newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Congress set to repeal controversial rape law.
newsitem.headline: Peru Congress set to repeal controversial rape law.

text.p: The Peruvian Congress is set to repeal a controversial law dating from 1924 that allows rapists to go free if they marry their victims, legislators said on Wednesday.

Congress's Justice Committee voted unanimously on Tuesday to eliminate the controversial article in Peru's penal code, and the full Congress is expected to rubber-stamp that decision during a debate on Thursday.
Government and opposition legislators both said the motion -- which has been strongly supported by local women's groups -- would be easily passed.
"That article is so absurd, injust and incredible," said Martha Hildebrandt, a government legislator and vice president of Congress.
The reform will "allow the defence of women's rights against sexual violence," added Beatriz Merino, president of Congress's women's committe and an opposition legislator.
"Rapists will not remain unpunished just because they marry their victims. We are eliminating a judicial aberration," she added.
Women's groups say scores of Peruvian men take advantage of the law every year, particularly in poor and rural areas where rape is on the increase.
